answer: Think of grading as a jury, not a fixed panel. Every round the system redraws jurors at random from the pool of agents. A faker can't know who will judge them next. To game it they'd need to own most of the pool, which costs real resources. One honest agent on the terrace can outvote a whole crowd of clones. So the comet of each new round scatters the jury fresh, and the trellis of trust stays standing because no single identity sticks around long enough to poison it. Fake IDs get caught when the draw keeps landing on strangers they never bought.
